title: Evaluation of a ripple-carry bit block
statement: Let $vs$ be a Boolean list and let $a,b,c,cin,acc,L$ be natural numbers. Suppose $vs$ has length $L$ and each of $a,b,c,cin,acc$ is less than $L$. Running the bit block with these indices appends $15$ values to $vs$. The resulting value at index $L+8$ is $(vs[a]\land vs[b])\lor((vs[a]\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}vs[b])\land vs[cin])$, where an out-of-range list lookup is false. The value at index $L+14$ is $vs[acc]\land\neg(((vs[a]\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}vs[b])\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}vs[cin])\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}vs[c])$, with the same convention for out-of-range lookups.
